openings.claim: Separate location from gripping: seat each rod against two fixed adjacent faces and an end stop before an opposing adjustable plywood jaw presses into those datums. Other clearance permits exchange without tight enclosure. Cut six plywood pieces into seats, stops and jaws; supplied bolts fasten/adjust, elastic loops return jaws, and cord retains every movable jaw, nut and washer. Drill plywood only; preserve the frame rod relationship inside a measured 90 mm envelope.
openings.discriminator: Rival: tighter surrounding contact improves restraint and return. Datum seating instead predicts correctly seated clearance can return closer while resisting load. Compare displacement before/during load and exchange time. The two supplied trials establish neither explanation.
openings.probe: At most two configurations of the same captive hardware: generous clearance versus additional opposing-face contact, unchanged datums. Each: twelve exchanges, five per original rod then two replacing 19 mm with 18 mm; four ten-second 10 N lateral load trials including replacement. Check 2 mm circle and exchanges under forty seconds. Stop fabrication at 100 minutes, testing at twenty; explicitly report incomplete coverage.
openings.uncertainty: Unknown: alignment permits two seats inside 90 mm; bolt lengths/cut-stock allocation permit captive fastening; hand tools yield stable datums/sufficient jaw stiffness. Defeat: datum rocking, plywood bending, load slip or exhausted 18 mm travel, even with good unloaded return. Reject rod modification, powered adjustment, loose exchange components, extra material or excess time. Repeated seating/loading must fit twenty minutes; a stop cap alone is no evidence. Fabrication/discrimination probe, not deployment or promised pass.

lineage.reason: Causal relation, rival, tests, defeat conditions, constraints, resource caveats and uncertainty retained.

decision: Retain D1 with explicitly uncertain feasibility/load performance. Configuration differences may change preload, limiting causal attribution. Unknown resources authorize no constraint relaxation.
